11.04pm Another nail-biter from Colombo. Bangladesh edge past India - the third time 
in four matches between the teams that the result has gone Bangladesh's way - even as 
India happily experimented after having already made the Asia Cup final. But take 
nothing away from Bangladesh: they were without Mushfiqur and Taskin, having already 
been hit by injuries earlier in the tournament. A win too late perhaps, but still a 
confidence booster ahead of the World Cup. Hang around for the presentations. 
Tanzim Hasan: "First wicket of Rohit bhai was a dream wicket. I just concentrate on line 
and length. I mentally prepare myself for a long spell. That ball (the last ball to Shami), I 
believed I could bowl the perfect ball. Very good feeling." 
Rohit Sharma after the tight loss: "We wanted to give some game time to the guys, 
keeping the bigger picture in mind. Not compromising on how we wanted to play this 
game. Get in some players who are likely to play the World Cup. Axar batted brilliantly, 
but couldn't finish. He showed a lot of character. But credit to the Bangladesh bowlers. 
Not to forget, Gill's hundred was brilliant. He backs his game; he knows exactly how he 
wants to play. Pretty clear on what he wants to do for the team. Look at his form over 
the last year. Pretty solid against the new ball. Works really hard; there's no optional 
practice for Gill." 
Habib: "With their top pace trio (Taskin, Hasan Mahmud and Shoriful), Tamim and 
Mushfiq missing, it's a big win for Bangladesh." 
Zia: "@Habib: don't forget about Shanto and Ebadot" 
Time for the presentations 
Shakib Al Hasan is the Player of the Match: "We gave [chances] to the guys who haven't 
played much. We thought spinners will play a part, and luckily they did. I wasn't batting 
well during this Asia Cup, but today I had time to settle. When I hit my first boundary, it 
felt good. When the ball got older, spin was difficult to play. When Mahedi came on, it 
wasn't easy to bowl. He bowled five overs in a row in the end. I should give credit to 
Sakib (Tanzim) also. I think we have got a very good team [for the World Cup]. Lot of 
injuries, and players coming in and going out didn't help during this Asia Cup." 
Geo: "It is not as if this is a completely second-string Indian team - other than Tilak and 
Prasidh, everyone else has loads of experience with them....so it is very, very good for 
Bangladesh!" 
So Bangladesh fight their way to a close win despite Gill's 121. India's batting line-up, 
missing only Kohli among the regulars, fell just short of chasing 266 to give Bangladesh 
a consolation win. Sidharth Monga's report details the rest of it. Now there's only one 
match to go in this year's Asia Cup. Sri Lanka will host India in the final on Sunday. But 
before that comes, you can also follow New Zealand's chase against England, and 
Australia's attempt to climb Mount 417 vs South Africa. Until next time, this is 
Himanshu signing off on behalf of Monga, Thilak and Raghav! Good night!
